headline: Structure-aware statistical methods for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics inference
label: Single Cell Statistical Methods
summary: New inference frameworks model zero inflation, longitudinal participant structure, and spatial dependence in single-cell data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is statistical inference tailored to the structure of single-cell and spatial measurements rather than generic models. QuasiMed performs quasi-regression mediation analysis for zero-inflated single-cell data without strict distributional assumptions. sctrial provides participant-level differential analysis of longitudinal scRNA-seq with calibrated error rates in simulations, and block-SAM respects nested sample structure in mass spectrometry imaging and scRNA-seq. In spatial transcriptomics and tissue imaging, GP-GHS infers spatially varying cell-cell interaction networks using HSGP coefficients and group horseshoe priors, while a counterfactual directionality score and a geometry-aware ligand-receptor framework separate directional influence and interface association from spatial localization. A benchmark of nine cell-cell interaction tools on simulated and real spatial datasets adds a comparative reference point. The novelty lies in explicit modeling of spatial variation, directionality, and hierarchical sample design.
